description.narrative: The Balkan Investigative Reporting Network (BIRN) Hub aims to contribute to a society that upholds demoeratic values and freedoms allowing citizens equal opportunities to make informed choices and hold governments accountable through investigative reporting.

The Balkan Investigative Reporting Network (BIRN) Hub syftar till att bidra till ett samhälle med demokratiska värderingar och friheter som möjliggör lika möjligheter för medborgare att fatta informerade beslut och att hålla sina regeringar ansvariga genom undersökande journalistik.

The Society upholds democratic values and freedoms allowing citizens equal opportunities to make informed choices and hold governments accountable.
Outcome objectives: 1. Access to accurate information increased and people in power kept accountable 2. Democratic processes strengthened and public enabled to make informed decisions, demand or influence change 3. Media and CSOs transformed and empowered with skills and knowledge to effectively address public interest 4. BIRN's journalistic archive and tools systemized and made available for further examination, advocacy and learning 5. BIRN grew into a learning and knowledge sharing organisation promoting high-quality journalism production and good governance

Previous results - BIRN's key web pages had almost 6,5 million unique visitors in 2023, nearly 819 000 subscribers on facebook, 91 000 on Instagram, 176 000 on Twitter/X, 99 000 on youtube. - BIRN journalists received several awards from RYCO, the EU and various national associations and included journalists from BIRN Kosovo, Bosnia, Serbia and North Macedonia. - published 17 418 articles - conducted 206 investigations - produced five documentaries - 30 trainings with 473 participants - 7 workshops with 113 participants on investigative journalisme and media freedom - 240 journalists participated in mentorship, on the job training - 103 grants/fellowships/awards/scholarships awarded to support independent media (76 to individuals, 23 to media outlets, 4 to CSOs) - many calls from national and international organizations to follow up reporting in Bosnia for instance. These were demands from individuals and organisations for further investigation on the role of Greek fighters in the Bonsia war 1995. The Engaged Citizens Reporting (ECR) tool developed to gather information from the public generated articles in North Macedonia. - BIRN one of very few organisations reporting on digital rights in the region (Reporting Digital Rights and Freedoms) with its most recent annual report (December 2023) documenting 1 427 digital rights violation cases. - BIRN Serbia contributed to public discussions on new media legislation, including submitting amendments to the Law on Public Information. - BIRN maintain and update six databases that monitors media ownership, and expanded their use for education, research and advocacy.
Results from 2024 BIRN's investigative journalism was widespread and well-known. BIRN's work has had a demonstrated effect on the ground and at times have lead to, or at least contributed to, changes visible in the society, such as exposed high-level corruption leading to imprissonment or judicial processes being initiated, cleaning of illeagal dumps, opening critical discussions and leading to political demands, revised decisions by institutions, institutional changes within Europol.
BIRN's work was used by civil society for further advocacy work and awareness raising. Investigations have sparked action from civil society such as sending petitions, legal actions, and broad public campaigning. Exhibitions by BIRN have spurred public interest and requests for more information. Research and investigations have also led to development of policy papers and recommendations, for instance BIRN Montenegro on assets declaration of public officials with special emphasis on crypto and digital assets.
BIRN has built capacity for local media and the network has participated in and contributed to cross-border investigations.
Key results 2024 include: - 26 140 articles - 178 TV shows and documentaries - 148 investigations - More than 2500 Freedom of Information requests - 19 conferences/public events organised - 31 episodes of podcasts produced - 650 short videos produced - 8 databases and maps updated - 2 new databases developed - 1716 cases of digital rights violations monitored - 21 awards in 2024 Web and social media statistics: - Almost 10 million unique visitors - More than 26 million web page views on BIRN Network's websites
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
